newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southwest spot power down amid cool weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southwest spot power down amid cool weather.

text.p: Spot power prices in the U.S. Southwest fell today amid below-normal temperatures which are expected to continue for the remainder of the month, traders said Tuesday.
"It's 10 degrees below normal in southern Arizona," said a Tucson trader. "Loads are way down."
Next-day prices at the Palo Verde substation in Arizona were last quoted $16.50-17.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), down from $17.50-19.50 on Monday.
Off-peak Palo Verde power traded today at $11.00, according to market sources.
In the Northwest, spot power for peak loads held fairly steady from Monday at $14.50-15.00 per MWh, while off-peak prices were around $12.00.
October COB was assessed at $15.45-15.65, compared with $15.45-15.75 on Monday. Palo Verde for October was quoted 15.80-15.90, compared with Monday's 15.60-15.90.
Sources said the possible outage of a 1,070-MW unit at the San Onofre nuclear generating station in southern California could help stabilize prices, but the situation remains uncertain.
Southern California Edison Co, the majority owner and operator of the nuclear plant, said the unit definitely will not be shut this week, but it remains under close scrutiny.

Edison contemplated shutting the unit later this week for two weeks of maintenance, but for now will continue to closely monitor pressure indications for water seals on one of the unit's four reactor pumps, said spokesman Ray Golden.
The same nuclear unit is also scheduled to start a 65-day refueling outage at the end of November.
- D Beasley, New York power desk + 213-859-1628
